chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar all narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hussein narrated to me through a chain of his own which he links up (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

He will not enter Paradise: the one who frequently drinks wine (alcoholic), the haughty/arrogant, the dutiful-to-parents-failer (unfilial), the one with intensely black hair, the pimp, the detective (Qallaa), the effeminate (Zanooq), the grave robber (Khayuf), the tax collector (Ashar), the one who severs kinship ties, and the Qadarite (determinist).

The compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: What is meant by 'intensely black' is the one whose head hair and beard hair do not turn white despite his advanced age, and he is called 'al-Gharib' (the stranger/outlander).

key_terms.الْغَرِيبَ: The stranger / one distinct in appearance
key_terms.دِيوثٌ: Pimp / one who exposes women's chastity
key_terms.قَلَّاعٌ: Detective / one who seeks out faults
key_terms.مُدْمِنُ خَمْرٍ: Alcoholic / one who frequently drinks wine

ai.seo_question: Who are the ten people that will not enter Paradise according to this hadith from Al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq enumerates ten distinct categories of individuals excluded from Paradise, linking specific moral and social vices—such as alcoholism, arrogance, and severing kinship ties—to spiritual ruin. The compiler’s gloss on 'intensely black' (Shadid al-Sawad) as the 'Westerner' (Gharib) who retains black hair into old age reflects a classical exegetical tradition interpreting physical distinctiveness as a marker of character or status. This list serves as a comprehensive ethical framework in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing both internal piety and external social conduct.
